job.title: Data Engineer, Flex Analytics
job.pay_full: $101,300 – $160,000 a year base salary (Bellevue), plus sign-on payments and restricted stock units

details.about: The Amazon Flex Analytics team is building the global business intelligence platform behind Amazon Flex. This Data Engineer helps the team use data to understand Flex driver behavior and satisfaction, building the analytics technology that gives teams flexible, structured access to their data: a BI platform, metrics and KPIs, and automated reporting and visualization.
duties: Create and support data pipelines on Amazon and AWS technologies including Spark, Glue, Kinesis and Redshift/Spectrum
Improve the data architecture, data quality, monitoring and data availability
Work with BI Engineers to improve reporting and analysis and simplify self-service support
Design, implement and support platforms that give business teams ad-hoc access to large datasets
Design scalable processes to publish data and reconcile data sets for integrity and accuracy
Take part in planning discussions that drive the data engineering team's work
needs: Experience with data modeling, warehousing and building ETL pipelines
Experience with one or more query languages (e.g. SQL, PL/SQL, DDL, MDX, HiveQL, SparkSQL, Scala)
Experience with one or more scripting languages (e.g. Python, KornShell)
nice: Big data technologies such as Hadoop, Hive, Spark or EMR
Any ETL tool such as Informatica, ODI, SSIS, BODI or Datastage
Python, R or Spark experience is highly preferred
details.benefits: Base salary $101,300 – $160,000 a year (Bellevue). The package includes sign-on payments and restricted stock units (RSUs); final pay depends on experience, qualifications and location. Benefits include medical, dental, vision and prescription cover, life and AD&D insurance, mental health support, flexible spending accounts, adoption and surrogacy reimbursement, 401(k) matching, paid time off and parental leave.
notes: Amazon offers workplace accommodations during the hiring process for candidates with disabilities
